subject: Exec authorization request — hosted API concession for AstraLumen
messages:
From: Kate Liu <kate@astralumen.ai>
To: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, procurement@astralumen.ai
Date: 2028-05-10T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Hosted API pricing & contract questions

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for walking us through the demo last week. We loved the latency profiles and the billing clarity. Our procurement team did an initial run and asked if Redwood can provide a 30% discount vs published Hosted API consumption rates for a 24-month commitment at our projected volumes (~2.5B tokens/month after ramp).

What AstraLumen can offer in exchange: 24-month committed spend (prepaid quarterly), permissive case study + logo, and a joint PR once we go live in Q4. We'd also like a 99.9% uptime SLA and a regional routing guarantee (US-east primary).

Can you confirm whether a concession at that depth is possible and what additional contract terms you'd require?

Thanks,
Kate
Kate Liu
Head of Procurement, AstraLumen

--
AstraLumen | enabling clinical decisioning with safer models
From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Kate Liu <kate@astralumen.ai>
Cc: ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-10T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing & contract questions

Kate — really appreciate the clarity and the case study offer.

Short answer: 30% off list is outside our standard delegation for Hosted API; anything >20% requires Exec authorization. I wanted to loop in Ben (head of sales ops) and Karthik (deal desk lead) to surface the business case and recommended concessions from our side.

Proposed internal mitigation that would make a deeper concession palatable:
- 24-month minimum term, prepaid quarterly
- 12-month ramp schedule with committed minimums (so actual discount floors in early months)
- Dedicated support package (Redwood Premier) rather than standard support
- Case study & public reference within 6 months of launch
- We reserve the right to route >5% of traffic to a compatible, lower-cost variant if capacity constraints arise (technical fallback)

I've attached their SOW and a draft pricing grid they sent. Ben/Karthik — can you advise recommended approval amount and the exact ask we should present to execs? I can draft the ask email once we decide the recommended concession and the guardrails.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: AstraLumen_SOW_v2.pdf, pricing_grid_v3.xlsx
From: ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-11T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing & contract questions

Marissa / Karthik — reading this, I think the ask is strategic (healthcare reference + long term commitment) but 30% is a stretch from list. Data points:
- Published comps: larger deals typically land 15–22% after committed volume and prepayment
- We have precedent for 25% on multi-year strategic plays where there's a unique product fit + ref/case study

My recommended ask to execs: approval to grant up to 25% off list conditioned on: 24-month prepay, 6-mo performance milestone (latency & error rate), and standard data protection annex + SOC2 evidence. If execs want to push to 30% we need a stronger upside: additional marketing commitment and a firm multi-year spend guarantee (not just projection).

Karthik — can you model the unit economics for 25% vs 30% across their projected token curve and flag the break-even/cash impact? I can draft the ask note for Mina and the leadership team once we have those numbers.

Ben
VP, Sales Operations
From: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-12T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing & contract questions

Ben / Marissa — ran the numbers. Quick summary:
- Baseline list: $0.012 / 1k tokens (example list rate)
- Projected monthly tokens (month 6 steady state): 2.5B tokens => $30k/month @ list (math simplified to per-1M tokens scale for modeling)
- At 25% concession our blended gross margin drops ~14% against current hosted mix; at 30% it's ~20% lower.
- With prepaid quarterly and committed minimums, the short-term cash improves materially which mitigates margin erosion, but long-term unit economics only work if we keep caching + batching optimizations and route heavy tails to quantized variants when appropriate.

Recommendation: Submit a formal exec ask for up to 25% with the following guardrails in the term sheet: prepaid quarterly, 24-month minimum, committed monthly floors, Redwood Premier support, and a customer success playbook tied to model optimization.

I'll attach a short model (separate). If leadership wants to entertain 30% we should require a stronger financial guarantee (accelerator clause + marketing minimum spend).

Karthik
Deal Desk Lead
From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: mina_haddad <mina@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-15T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Exec approval request: AstraLumen Hosted API concession (seeking up to 25%)

Mina — looping you in for authorization. Below is a concise ask with recommended guardrails.

What we need from Execs: authorization to grant AstraLumen up to 25% off published Hosted API consumption rates. Anything >20% requires explicit signoff.

Why:
- Strategic customer in clinical decisioning; strong reference opportunity and co-marketing ask (joint PR).
- 24-month prepaid commitment (quarterly installments) and an initial committed floor that reduces tail-risk during ramp.
- They expect 2.5B tokens/month steady state; our modeling (attached) shows 25% is acceptable with prepaid and CS optimization.

Proposed commercial terms (summary):
- Discount: up to 25% off list (final % TBD by finance once legal confirms contract clauses)
- Term: 24 months, prepaid quarterly
- Minimums: Month 1-3 floor = 15% of projected steady-state each month; month 4-12 ramp to steady state
- Support: Redwood Premier (dedicated CSM, 24x5 response)
- SLA: 99.9% uptime; regional routing guarantee (US-east primary)
- Deliverables: case study & one public reference within 6 months of launch
- Opt-out protections: Right to migrate small % of traffic to compatible, lower-cost variants during severe capacity constraints

Attachments: modeled P&L (pricing_grid_v3.xlsx), SOW (AstraLumen_SOW_v2.pdf).

Approve/Decline/Modify? If you approve, I'll prepare the final ask email to execs and route a redline with Legal for the special concession appendix.

Thanks,
Marissa
From: mina_haddad <mina@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-16T17:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exec approval request: AstraLumen Hosted API concession (seeking up to 25%)

Team — I support granting up to 25% for this opportunity with the guardrails you've outlined. A few notes:

1) Limit the approved concession to 25% exactly (not a range). Any ask beyond 25% must come back to me with a finance-side P&L and a legal-approved append (we will not go >25% without CFO sign-off).
2) Prepayment schedule must be non-refundable for the first 12 months in order to mitigate churn during their ramp.
3) Require a short accelerator clause: if AstraLumen exceeds projected volumes by >40% for two consecutive quarters, they lose the concession for new incremental volume (standardized to prevent open-ended exposure).
4) Legal to prepare an appendix capturing the routing fallback and the SLA terms. No changes to our standard data handling obligations.

Marissa — proceed to finalize the term sheet with Legal and Procurement; Ben/Karthik, please confirm the P&L model assumptions are reflected in the final ask. I'll sign the final concession authorization once Legal confirms the appendix language.

Mina
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

--
Approved: concession = 25% off published Hosted API consumption rates (subject to Legal appendix and Finance confirmation)
